title: Blueprints `sk-prop-sf-pf-coherence` and `sk-thm-sf-package` (clause (2)): the coherence of the composition law for `Rf_!` with the projection formula
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. For every scheme $T$, work in the ordinary unbounded derived category $D_T=D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with exact inverse image $f^*=f^{-1}$ and ordinary derived tensor [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, def-kun-derived-tensor]. For every morphism $f:X\to Y$ supplied with a chosen compactification $X\xrightarrow{j_f}\overline X_f\xrightarrow{p_f}Y$ ($j_f$ open, $p_f$ proper, $p_fj_f=f$) [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-proper-morphism], put $F_f=Rp_{f*}Dj_{f!}:D_X\to D_Y$. Open parts need not be quasi-compact and schemes need not be Noetherian. Let $\pi_f(M,N):F_fM\otimes^LN\to F_f(M\otimes^Lf^*N)$ be the canonical proper counit-defined projection map followed by the open tensor comparison [lem-sf-etale-ambient-adjoint-projection, def-kun-projection-formula-map, lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor]. For a Cartesian square [def-pc-fibre-product] with maps $a:X'\to X$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $f:X\to Y$, $b:Y'\to Y$ and quasi-compact $f'$, let $\operatorname{Ex}_f:b^*F_f\to F_{f'}a^*$ be the specified rightDerivedLowerShriekBaseChangeMap: proper unit--square--counit exchange, inverse open base-change mate, then the canonical comparison from the pulled-back compactification to the chosen one [def-kun-unbounded-exchange, lem-asd-open-base-change-unit-mate, lem-pur-etale-graph-comparison-base-change].
There is one family of natural isomorphisms $E_{f,g,h,w}:F_h\xrightarrow{\sim}F_gF_f$, for all scheme maps $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$, $h:X\to Z$, $w:gf=h$, and all supplied compactifications of $f,g,h$, with both following properties.
(1) For every $M\in D_X$, $N\in D_Z$, writing $\gamma_N:h^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*g^*N$ for the canonical pullback compositor,
$$F_g(\pi_f(M,g^*N))\circ\pi_g(F_fM,N)\circ(E_M\otimes1_N)
=F_gF_f(1_M\otimes\gamma_N)\circ E_{M\otimes h^*N}\circ\pi_h(M,N).$$
(2) For any three Cartesian squares $(a,f',f,b)$, $(b,g',g,c)$ and $(a,h',h,c)$, with $a:X'\to X$, $b:Y'\to Y$, $c:Z'\to Z$, $g'f'=h'$, and compactifications of $f',g',h'$, suppose $f',g',h'$ are quasi-compact. For every $M\in D_X$,
$$E'_{a^*M}\circ\operatorname{Ex}_h(M)
=F_{g'}(\operatorname{Ex}_f(M))\circ\operatorname{Ex}_g(F_fM)\circ c^*(E_M),$$
where $E'=E_{f',g',h',w'}$ is from the same family. Both sides are maps $c^*F_hM\to F_{g'}F_{f'}a^*M$, with canonical associators inserted. No boundedness, constructibility, finite Tor-amplitude, invertibility of residue characteristics, or quasi-compactness of $f,g,h$ is added.

theorem exists_rightDerivedLowerShriekCompIso :
    ∃ E : ∀ {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (h : X ⟶ Z), f ≫ g = h →
        ∀ [HasCompactification f] [HasCompactification g] [HasCompactification h],
        R(h)_![ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ] ≅ R(f)_![ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ] ⋙ R(g)_![ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ],
      (∀ {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (h : X ⟶ Z) (w : f ≫ g = h)
        [HasCompactification f] [HasCompactification g] [HasCompactification h],
        Adjunction.ProjectionCompCompatible
          (fun M N ↦ ((projectionMap (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f).app M).app N)
          (fun M N ↦ ((projectionMap (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) g).app M).app N)
          (fun M N ↦ ((projectionMap (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) h).app M).app N)
          (fun N ↦ (leftDerivedUpperStarComp _ f g h w.symm).hom.app N) (E f g h w)) ∧
      (∀ {X Y Z X' Y' Z' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y ⟶ Z} {h : X ⟶ Z} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
        {g' : Y' ⟶ Z'} {h' : X' ⟶ Z'} {a : X' ⟶ X} {b : Y' ⟶ Y} {c : Z' ⟶ Z}
        (sqf : IsPullback a f' f b) (sqg : IsPullback b g' g c) (sqh : IsPullback a h' h c)
        (w : f ≫ g = h) (w' : f' ≫ g' = h') [HasCompactification f] [HasCompactification g]
        [HasCompactification h] [HasCompactification f'] [HasCompactification g']
        [HasCompactification h'] [QuasiCompact f'] [QuasiCompact g'] [QuasiCompact h'],
        Adjunction.ExchangeCompCompatible (rightDerivedLowerShriekBaseChangeMap Λ sqf)
          (rightDerivedLowerShriekBaseChangeMap Λ sqg) (rightDerivedLowerShriekBaseChangeMap Λ sqh)
          (E f g h w) (E f' g' h' w')) :=
  sorry

tool_uses.why: Steps 1-3 use its precise graph-factorization choice of E and its second (inverse-projection composition) identity on ordinary unbounded finite-ring etale categories. It carries all of the projection coherence calculation, which Step 3 inverts. The CBC unit has no projection/compositor identity: this is the independent projection-pentagon input below the fixed graph/compactification route, not a substitute for the CBC proof.

Step 1 uses its specified product of proper parts, two open neighborhoods, intersection and natural graph comparison for a supplied proper/open/proper presentation. The CBC unit has no unrestricted non-quasi-compact graph-model statement. This supplies concrete endpoint maps, not another proof of compact-support base change.

Step 3 takes only invertibility of the specified proper-counit/open-tensor compactification projection map on every unbounded input. Its adjoint/dualizing assertions are unused. The CBC unit supplies neither this projection-isomorphism fact nor a way to invert the projection identity.

Step 4 uses vertical/horizontal pasting and change of adjunctions for mates to verify exchange squares of proper and open compositors. This generic categorical identity has no coefficient or boundedness restriction and no counterpart in the CBC unit statements; it is applied to individual factors, not to assume the desired compact-support composition equation.
